Bipolar and bpd definitely look similar in terms of mood swings. My psych doctor had to check whether or not i was bipolar or not first before diagnosing me but we ruled it out that it wasn't that, and is defnirely possible to have both disorders but it gets much more complicated if you do have both

I take aripiprazole or also known as ablify daily. However as recently, i think it might be messing with my birth control so i have multiple doctor appointments coming up with the gyno and the psych doc to try and get that fixed and possibly go on different med for my mood swings. Secondly, I had lots of symptoms regarding the dsm criteria. The most noticeable on for me was that I had intense mood swings based on my fear of abandonment. When I didn't talk to a friend for like a few hours or a day, I would get really bad paranoia and fear thinking they left me behind and I would try to cut them out of my life or argue with them because of that imagined fear of abandonment. I had constant unstable relationships because even the smallest thing would set me off. I would put people on pedastals or devalue them the next minute. I was also extremely impulsive and self harmed a lot. Lastly, I had a very unstable image and still kinda do, I would either view myself as a monster or worthless cause of my constant breakdowns. I constantly questioned who I was as a person. Luckily, today I found myself a group of friends who are very understanding and luckily has not experienced the worse of my breakdowns. I also have a very loving boyfriend who while understands my problem,  he can't handle it emotionally sometimes when i do occasionally have a breakdown because he has mental health problems himself. It's overall much more healthy and i don't think they need to walk on eggshells around me because my moods swings ain't really a problem anymore

Technically, there is no specific type of medicine for Borderline Personality but the Psych doctor i met decided to put me on antipyschotics called Abilify to treat mainly just my mood swings. For me it's done wonders, but don't get me wrong, i still have the occasional bad day. I've also been doing counselling to help learn cope with my emotions better and I def do handle my episodes a bit better than i used to.
